subject.title: [Feature]: Add per-channel identity override for Discord bindings

question: Should OpenClaw support ordinary Discord routed-reply visible identity overrides for bindings, and should that be implemented as webhook persona delivery, bot self-profile mutation, a binding nickname field, or deferred?
rationale: The requested behavior creates new public config/API and bot-credential-backed identity behavior, and current source only has thread-bound webhook persona plus presence/status behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent identity/security contract.

options.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
options.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path using webhook username/avatar delivery with explicit secret handling, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Coordinate with self-profile work
options.body: Treat this as part of the Discord self-profile decision and add nickname/avatar mutation only if maintainers accept the guild-scoped identity semantics and security boundary.

options.title: Defer per-binding identity
options.body: Keep current bot-account replies plus thread-bound webhook persona behavior and ask users to use existing thread-bound flows or multiple bot accounts for now.

recommendation.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
recommendation.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path using webhook username/avatar delivery with explicit secret handling, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their thread-bound Discord subagents work owns the closest existing webhook/persona delivery model for this product choice.
